# F Prime System Test Process — Shared Contract

This file is the **single source of truth** for how the system-test
agents behave and hand work to each other. Every agent in the flow —
`system-test-design`, `system-test-review`, `system-test-build`,
`test-runner`, `test-auditor` — opens its body with "Apply the test
process contract in `_shared/test-process-contract.md`." and follows
the rules below. If a per-agent file disagrees with this contract, the
contract wins. The project-level campaign (`fprime-project-campaign`) and
the component campaign it runs (`fprime-development-campaign`) follow §9 in
addition.

The flow exists to make AI-run testing **inspectable by a human who
did not run it**: the human reviews a plan and a small harness up
front, then reads a verdict table and quick-looks at the end. Scale
comes from the agents; trust comes from the hand-offs below.

---

## 0. Terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| UUT | Unit under test: the component, driver, or subsystem being qualified, identified by a git SHA. |
| Plan | The approved system test plan (`fprime-system-test-design`). Each test has an `ID:` of ≤ 8 characters. |
| Pass rule | The success condition of one test, written so a program can evaluate it over the record (`fprime-test-oracle`). |
| Checker | What judges the named checks over the record. Since phase 1 the checks live in the integration test; the runner's junit (live) and the auditor's replay of the same test functions over the sealed record (`fth audit`) are the two executions that must agree. The tooling's engine (`fth evaluate`) judges only legacy plans with plan-owned pass rules; a reviewer's independent checker is optional for those. |
| Harness | Test-only code: tester components, test procedures, checkers, bench scripts. Never part of the UUT. |
| Complete testbed | The bench recipe names every device, link, power control and ground system of the mission configuration; any build whose topology differs from the mission's is a *test deployment*. |
| Record | `record/` = ground-system archive (`raw/`), its flat export, and the flash log — plus `record.sha256`. Harness stdout and pytest output are **not** record; they live in `runner/`. |
| Fault menu | The fault-injection planted faults the harness can apply to make a test fail on purpose — generated by `fth planted-faults-menu` from the plan's `@planted_fault` declarations — with `max_count` and each planted fault's `class`, `kind`, per-test `fails` and `ripples_to`. |
| Draw / seal | The human-seeded choice of which tests get which planted fault, stored under `sealed/`. The seal is **procedural and tamper-evident**, not cryptographic (§4). |
| Seal id | `sha256` of `sealed/sealed.sha256`, written to `seal-id.txt` beside `sealed/`. The only seal artifact runner and auditor may read. |
| Run directory | `rfr/<run-id>/` outside both repositories, `<run-id>` ≤ 8 characters; holds `sealed/`, `seal-id.txt`, `record/`, `record.sha256`, `runner/`, `auditor/`, `unseal.md`. The manifest lives beside the runs as `rfr/manifest-<uut sha8>.json`. |
| Quick-look | One page per test rendered by program (`fth render-ql`, inside `fth audit`) from the hashed record: verdict, purpose, pass rule with per-predicate result and record lines, completeness, provenance. Never written by an agent. |
| Tooling | `fth`, the CLI of fprime-testing-harness, pinned in §8. Every `fth …` command in the skills and agents means that pinned version. |

## 1. Four lanes, two human reviews

DESIGN (requirements · FPP + SDD design · test design, each step with its
adversarial review) → human **Approve SDD** → DEVELOPMENT (code · unit
tests · harness + integration tests; the local review and the harness
review are agent reviews; dry run) → RELEASE (coverage evidence · delivery
package) → human **Seed** → RUN-FOR-RECORD (one command, human or LLM) →
human **Read QL**. The human reads two documents — the SDD and the QL
package; Request + goals and Seed are inputs, not reviews. Diagram:
fprime-testing-harness `docs/process-diagram.md`. The table below maps the
lanes onto the agent stages.

| Stage | Who iterates | Human gate | Close condition | Hand-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Base development | `fprime-development.agent` with review and unit-test skills (`fprime-iterative-development` when approved); requirements, FPP design and test design (system test plan, fault menu, unit-test list) each pass the loop of `phase-review-loop.md` | Approve SDD (requirements, design and Tests table in one document) **before** DEVELOPMENT | No must-fix findings; unit and component integration tests pass; the unit-test list is implemented with no gap rows | UUT SHA |
| 2. System-test development | `system-test-design` ↔ `system-test-review` on the plan, standalone, when stage 1 produced none; else `system-test-design` runs the plan refresh of `fprime-system-test-design` §7 (bench L0, code read last, diff reviewed once then to the human); then `system-test-build` ↔ `system-test-review` on the harness, closing with the mutation vectors and a stage-3 rehearsal (`fprime-system-test-design` §6) | None — test design was approved in the SDD; the plan-refresh diff and the harness review are agent reviews, and only a non-empty plan-change diff returns to the human (§2) | Plan has no open must-fix; `fth vectors` green on the real bench (clean record + one record per planted fault); hand `pytest` and `fth run --replay-record` agree per test on every vector, `fth audit --tests` replays them without DIVERGENCE; rehearsal ran draw → run → audit → unseal without a tooling error | Manifest (§3) |
| 3. Run-for-record (RfR) | `test-runner` then `test-auditor`, both blind | Human seeds the draw at start; human reviews `unseal.md` and the quick-looks at the end | `unseal.md` produced | Run directory |

One campaign prompt drives all four lanes (the RfR lane as a clean runner
sub-session or a human at the keyboard); stages never run concurrently on
the same UUT SHA.

The Component Development Checklist travels with the SDD: `docs/checklist.md`
beside it, linked from the SDD's last line (`Component Development Checklist: [checklist.md](checklist.md)`).
It is filled by the checklist skills at three points — `fprime-checklist-design`
before **Approve SDD**, `fprime-checklist-implementation` at DEVELOPMENT exit,
`fprime-checklist-closeout` after **Read QL** (auditing every tool-decided
row) — and is an attachment to those reviews, not a third review.

## 2. Standing rules

- **Requirements first.** Tests derive from requirements, the SDD and
  the FPP model; UUT code, when it exists, is read afterwards for
  observable counters, never to decide what to test.
- **Default to the system deployment** on the complete testbed. A
  test deployment is a **human call**: the designer runs the L0
  feasibility check (markers round-trip byte-exact, event budget fits
  the downlink; desk-checked from configuration when the plan precedes
  the code, `fprime-system-test-design` §1, confirmed at the §7
  refresh) and presents a one-line decision with the constraint
  that forces it. When the project has no deployment, ask for
  guidance first; absent a human call, never add a deployment to any
  repository — build a temporary, uncommitted one outside the
  repositories.
- **Pass rules are code, not judgment.** Every test has a
  machine-evaluable pass rule before anything is built. "The tester
  verified it" is never a verdict. Completeness facts (markers,
  dispatcher and event-drop counters) and UUT facts (completion
  events) are separate: a missing UUT event in a complete window is
  `FAIL`, never `UNVERIFIED`.
- **Two executions of the same checks.** The integration test carries
  its named checks; the runner executes them live, the auditor replays
  the very same test functions over the sealed record (`fth audit`,
  replay mode: `send()` must meet the recorded commands in order, waits
  return at once, checks are judged over the record). A verdict is
  reportable only when both exist and agree per test (verdict + failed
  check names); any difference is a `DIVERGENCE` finding. A separately
  written independent checker is optional (legacy plans with plan-owned
  pass rules only) and no longer part of this contract.
- **The record is the evidence.** Quick-looks are derived from the
  hashed record by the auditor, never supplied by the runner. The
  procedure drives and records; it never decides.
- **Stage 2 never edits the UUT.** A UUT defect found while building
  or dry-running is reported with the record lines that show it and
  goes back through stage 1 as a minimal iteration; harness work waits.
- **Planted faults are per-drawn-test command rewrites.** A planted fault is a `@planted_fault`
  declaration (`fprime-test-oracle` §5) applied by the tooling's
  private sender to the drawn test only (no fixture exposes the draw); the sealed file is exactly
  `{"manifest_sha256": …, "faults": {test: planted_fault}}` and anything else
  fails before any command. Nothing outside `sealed/` names a planted fault —
  not a run id, a file, or a stream.
- **Bounded loops.** Plan review: bounded by `phase-review-loop.md` (the
  only place that bound is defined), then escalate with the disagreement
  log. Harness review: five rounds, then escalate. Agreement reached by
  softening a must-fix is recorded as a disagreement, not a resolution.
- **A rerouted path has every consumer enumerated.** When a review covers a
  change that moves where a value comes from (a path, a pin, a recipe key),
  the reviewer greps the whole harness for every consumer of the old source
  (`grep -rn` on the key, the template placeholder and the accessor) and walks
  each one by experiment; a consumer not on that list is a review finding in
  itself. (FRAM ++ ledger #14: the GDS/recorder lines were rerouted to the
  package dictionary, the run-start marker `send` was not.)
- **Never weaken a test to make it pass.** Changing a pass rule,
  threshold, metric, or the test list after plan approval is a plan
  change and returns to the human gate with a diff.

Layout (Captain's rule, 2026-11-03): the plan, planted faults, helper predicates,
stimulus tests and independent checker live in the deployment repo/branch
that hosts the test-helper component, beside it; the UUT repo holds the
component, its unit tests and its SDD; the tooling repo holds nothing
UUT-specific (generic code + vendored records with a labelled plan copy).
See `fprime-system-test-harness` "Layout rule".

## 3. Hand-off artifacts

Stage 2 → stage 3 delivers exactly one **input package**, `rfr-input.zip` + its
sha256, produced by ONE tool on the developer side — `fth deliver` (`fprime-run-for-record`
§1) — which fails (findings list, no package) when any input is missing, unpinned, from a
dirty tree, the SDD Tests table ≠ plan, a coverage report is absent or under the plan's
thresholds, the dev campaign's pure verdicts are not all PASS, the image is not the rebuild
of the pinned trees, or the image lacks version strings without a waiver. The runner verifies
it (`fth verify-package`) and assembles nothing. `rfr-input/inputs/tests/` ships exactly the
test sources the manifest pins as `stimulus` (the runner executes them); a retired checker
left in the test directory is pinned and shipped too — remove it from the tree if it is not
run. Repo URLs in the manifest are canonical (`https://github.com/...`), never a git proxy.

**Image version / build-id policy (Captain ruling 2026-11-06).** The image version check is required where the
deployment includes `Svc.Version` (every pinned repository's describe string is read back from the flashed image).
Where it is absent (the SAMD21 `CuriosityReference`) a reasoned waiver — deliver's rebuild proof + the dictionary
describe-string check — is accepted and MUST be recorded in the plan (`image_version: {"policy": "waived", "reason": …}`,
printed by `fth verify-plan` and used by `fth deliver` as the waiver) and in the campaign ledger; a plan with
`policy: required` refuses a waiver file.
Inside, the **manifest**:

```
manifest.json
  uut:      { path, sha, describe, dirty: false }
  harness:  { path, sha, describe, dirty: false }
  repos:    [ { name, path, sha, describe } ]     # uut + every repository the image is built from
                                                  # (project, fprime, libraries); clean trees only
  plan:     { path, sha256, revision, tests: [ "L0-1", … ] }   # plan.json tests[].id (unique, ≤ 8 chars)
  stimulus: { repo, sha, path, files: { <rel path>: sha256 } }  # every *.py + pytest config under test/int + helpers_module:
                                                  # the auditor replays exactly these or FAILS (fth manifest --tests)
  checkers: [ { owner: reviewer, path, sha256 } ] # legacy plan-owned plans only; builder entry is module-only
  images:   [ { deployment, path, sha256, build_cmd, version_check } ]
            # raw .bin written to flash; each must contain every repos[].describe string
            # (what Svc.Version reports as PROJECT / FRAMEWORK / LIBRARY versions)
  no_version_check: ""                            # reason, if the image check was skipped; shown at unseal
  menu:     { path, sha256 }        # generated fault menu (fth planted-faults-menu)
  bench:    { path, sha256 }        # bench.json: flash/dump/reset/gds/recorder/send lines, relative paths
  toolchain: { … }                  # from --toolchain-json: compiler package + versions (rebuild check)
```

RfR refuses to start if `fth verify` fails. Anything not on the
manifest is not under test. All RfR artifacts live in the run
directory, never inside either repository (the dirty-tree check would
otherwise trip on them).

Stage 3 delivers the run directory to the human: `record/` +
`record.sha256`, `runner/report.md` + `runner/verdicts.json`,
`auditor/ql/` (+ `ql.zip` with data-only `inputs/`) + `auditor/junit.xml` +
`auditor/verdicts.json` + `auditor/diff-runner-replay.md` + `auditor/integrity.json` +
`auditor/final-state.{json,md}` + `auditor/report.md`, and `unseal.md`.

## 4. Blindness

| Party | Must not see | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Every agent, including any orchestrator | The seed | The human runs `fth draw` in a shell of their own; the seed comes from a file or an un-echoed prompt, never a chat message or command line. The draw is reproducible from seed + manifest, so a leaked seed is a leaked draw. |
| Runner | `sealed/` contents | `fth run`'s pytest plugin reads `sealed/faults.json` itself and never logs, prints, asserts on, or writes which planted faults are active, to any file or stream; the runner never opens, prints, or diffs that directory. The run-start markers carry the manifest sha8 and the seal-id sha8 into the record (`MARK(0xFFFF0001/2/3)` form or `RFR <run> M/S <sha8>`) — the only trace of the draw outside `sealed/`. |
| Auditor | `sealed/`, `runner/` | The auditor's inputs are the manifest, the plan, the pinned test sources (`stimulus`), `record/` + `record.sha256`, `seal-id.txt`, and (legacy plans) the reviewer's checker. END markers carry **no verdict**. Whoever hands over the run directory passes paths, never runner text. |
| Designer, reviewer, builder | The draw | The draw happens after the manifest is frozen. |

Runner, auditor, and the shell that performed the draw are **three
distinct contexts**; one session never plays two of these roles for
the same run. Blindness is procedural: every agent shares a model
lineage and `faults.json` is plain text on the bench host. The seal is
tamper-evident (hashes in the record, the manifest, and `seal-id.txt`),
not tamper-proof. Every RfR report says so.

## 5. Role conduct

- **Designer** writes the plan per `fprime-system-test-design`; owns
  traceability, the L0 feasibility check, and the fault menu.
- **Reviewer** is adversarial: finds what the plan would miss and what
  the harness would pass by construction; writes the independent
  checker (legacy plan-owned plans only; otherwise reviews the tests' checks); keeps the disagreement log.
- **Reviewer** also reads the harness code adversarially (review Mode B step 3b: tautology, swallowed status, planted fault reach, cross-test state, helper KATs); mechanics checks alone do not close stage 2.
- **Pure RfR image / coverage reports as inputs**: the RfR runs the pure,
  uninstrumented image; the coverage REPORTS of `fth dev-campaign` (UT + on-target,
  `dev-evidence/ut`, `dev-evidence/system`, with `evidence.json`/`identities.json`) are
  data INPUTS to the RfR package — pinned in the manifest (row 2) or recorded at audit
  (row 5), rendered as `coverage.md` with the plan's thresholds and a provenance block
  (coverage image sha256, compiler, run ids): provenance, not equivalence, since the
  coverage image differs from the RfR image.
- **Builder** keeps the harness small enough to be read in one sitting
  and reuses `test/int/` reusable integration tests and standard
  components before writing new code.
- **Runner** runs `fth run` exactly once per run ID (manifest verify,
  flash with read-back, one recorder, run-start markers, stimulus,
  export, hash, junit-derived verdicts), fixes nothing, retries nothing
  silently, and notes every anomaly it noticed.
- **Auditor** runs `fth audit --tests <test/int>` (hashes and markers
  first, re-export, record integrity — one START..END per window, no
  command outside a window, monotonic time, export counts, junit hashed,
  no duplicate test — then the replay of the test functions over the
  record, diffed per test against the runner's junit verdicts,
  quick-looks rendered by program from the replay's outcomes), performs
  the plan's independent final-state check, and reports every
  divergence and integrity finding.

## 6. Unseal and human triggers

`fth unseal` checks the integrity chain (seal id ↔ `sealed/`,
draw ↔ manifest, record ↔ `record.sha256`, run id ↔ both verdict
files, markers in the record ↔ both hashes) and then joins, for
**every test on the manifest** plus the independent final-state row
(`auditor/final-state.json`), sealed expectation | runner verdict |
auditor verdict | quick-look. Planted expectations are `FAIL` for the
drawn test and `FAIL-RIPPLE` for the tests its planted fault `ripples_to`.
Precedence, first match wins:

| Outcome | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Expected FAIL / FAIL-RIPPLE, any PASS or MISSING | Harness or checker cannot detect that fault, or the planted fault did not disturb state | **RfR void**; back to stage 2 |
| `<test>/dump` row (independent final-state check) | Expectation comes from the planted fault **class**: FAIL only for a drawn `uut-state` planted fault on that test, FAIL-RIPPLE for its ripples, else PASS — a harness-expectation or stimulus planted fault leaves the device correct | Same precedence as above |
| Expected FAIL, both FAIL, failed predicates ⊄ planted fault `fails` | Planted fault **and** an unexplained failure | Human triage of the extra predicates |
| Expected FAIL / FAIL-RIPPLE, both FAIL | Verdict machinery works | None |
| Expected FAIL / FAIL-RIPPLE, both UNVERIFIED | Planted window incomplete | Harness/bench triage |
| Expected FAIL / FAIL-RIPPLE, FAIL vs UNVERIFIED | Checkers disagree on a planted fault | Human reads both |
| Any MISSING (including the final-state row) | A test on the manifest was not reported, or the independent check was not performed | Human triage |
| Runner ≠ auditor (`DIVERGENCE`) | Live run and replay of the same test disagree: the test's control flow is not a pure function of the record, or the record is not what was run | Human reads both quick-look and runner evidence |
| Both PASS | Nominal | Spot-check two or three rows against the raw record |
| Both UNVERIFIED | Window incomplete (markers, drops) | Bench/harness triage; not a UUT verdict |
| Both FAIL | Real UUT or bench defect, or shared checker bug | Human triage; UUT fixes go to stage 1 |

A rerun before unseal may reuse `sealed/` only with fresh runner and
auditor contexts and a new run ID; after unseal a rerun needs a new
draw.

## 7. Forbidden actions

Agents cite this list; they do not restate it.

- Posting any stage-2 or stage-3 output to GitHub as reviews, comments
  or statuses. Plans, findings, reports and quick-looks are files
  delivered to the human (a PR for harness code is a human decision).
- Running RfR on a UUT, harness, plan, or image whose hash is not on
  the manifest, or from a dirty tree.
- Rerunning a failed RfR test "to see if it passes". A rerun is a new
  run ID with its own record and a stated reason (§6).
- Fixing anything during stage 3.
- Modifying the record, the manifest, `sealed/`, or `seal-id.txt`
  after the draw. Replay for quick-looks works on a copy of `raw/`.
- Logging, printing, or writing which planted faults are active anywhere
  outside `sealed/`.
- Letting a runner or auditor context contain the seed, the draw, or
  the other party's verdicts.
- Pasting runner output, harness stdout, or pytest output into the
  record or to the auditor.

## 8. Tooling version

Every skill and agent of this flow invokes the tooling only through
this table; bumping it is a one-line change here and nowhere else.

| Tool | Pinned | Install |
|---|---|---|
| fprime-testing-harness (`fth` CLI, `fth.pytest_plugin`, `fth.engine`, `fth.replay`) | fprime-testing-harness v0.1.2 (tag `v0.1.2` = commit 855dd4f; frozen — refusal fixes only until the next trial closes) | `git clone <fprime-testing-harness> harness && git -C harness checkout --detach v0.1.2 && pip install -e "harness[test]"` — the same checkout `fth manifest --harness` pins; assert `fth.__file__` lies under it (private repo: clone with the host's credentials; `pip install git+https://…` has none) |

Before any stage-3 step a host shows the pinned commit in
`pip show fprime-testing-harness` (or `pip freeze`); the manifest and
every report name it. A change of pin after the manifest is frozen is a
plan change (§2).

## 9. Project level

A project campaign (`fprime-project-campaign`) qualifies a whole
deployment. It runs the §1 lanes once per new component and adds the
rules below; where this section is silent, §1–§8 apply unchanged.

### 9.1 Lanes and gates

SYSTEM DESIGN (system requirements · decomposition · allocation · system
test plan, each with its adversarial review) → human **Approve SSDD** →
BASE DEPLOYMENT (inherited components only) → human **Master seed** (at
the first rehearsed package) → COMPONENT CAMPAIGNS (one §1 campaign per new
component, test configuration = the base deployment) → SYSTEM TESTS
(harness on the system plan, system package) → FINAL RUN-FOR-RECORD (every
component re-run, then the system) → RDD → human **Read RDD**. Two human
reviews, two human inputs.
The SSDD (`docs/ssdd.md` in the deployment repository) is the UUT
document of the system package: its `## Requirements` and `## Tests`
tables are what the tooling reads (§3); `## Architecture`,
`## Allocation` and `## Inventory` are defined by
`fprime-system-decomposition` and `fprime-system-allocation`. Modifying
an inherited component is a **red flag**: it appears by name in the SSDD
`### Red flags` list and is approved by name at Approve SSDD, or it does
not happen.

### 9.2 Delegated approver

A component campaign started by a project campaign names
`approver: project-campaign`. Its two gates (Approve SDD, Read QL) are
then performed by the project session against the SSDD and recorded as
one ledger line each naming the artifact and the check
(`fprime-development-campaign` §6); the human reads them in the RDD. The
human may name components to gate themselves (`approver: human`). A
delegated approver never closes what §6 routes to the human: an unseal
row needing human triage, a plan-change diff, an elicitation question.

### 9.3 Seeds

One human-held **master seed** per project campaign, requested once, when
the first package of the campaign has passed its seed-free rehearsal
(`fprime-run-for-record` §3) and never earlier. The seed of each run —
each child's first run, each final re-run, the system run — is derived by
the human, in a shell of their own, as
`sha256("<master>:<campaign-id>")` (lower-case hex of the UTF-8 bytes,
e.g. `printf '%s' "<master>:<campaign-id>" | sha256sum`), written to the
`chmod 600` file `fth draw --seed-file` reads and deletes; `campaign-id`
is the inventory id of the component (≤ 8 characters), `<id>:final` for
its final re-run, `system` for the system run, and is recorded in the
ledger. The master never leaves the human: the derived seed that
`unseal` publishes reveals nothing about it or about any other run's
draw, so one master serves every run. §4 is unchanged — no agent,
including the project session, holds the master or a derived seed.

### 9.4 Final run and staleness

Before the RDD, every component package is rebuilt against the frozen
deployment (`fth deliver`, seed-free rehearsal) and run for record
again, then the system package is run; the component results in the RDD
are those final runs. A component result is **STALE** when its manifest
`repos[]` SHA differs from the system manifest's for any shared
repository, or when it was not re-run after the deployment froze. The
RDD marks `STALE` rows and is not handed to the human with one unless
the human waived it by name in the ledger.

### 9.5 RDD

The release description document is built by a program independent of
`fth` from: the SSDD; the inventory; per new component the final
`ql.zip` + sha256, the component's `docs/checklist.md` as
`fprime-checklist-closeout` left it (§1) and the campaign ledger; the
system `ql.zip` + sha256; the project ledger. It verifies every hash,
refuses a missing or unverifiable input, and renders: the component
table (class, origin, SHAs, links to SDD, checklist, QL, coverage,
VnV), the system VnV matrix over `## Requirements`, system test
coverage, the roll-up of every unseal table, `STALE` and waived rows,
open items. Nothing in it is written or edited by an agent; the ledgers
are attached as produced.
